contracts.userOutcome: A keyboard move across journal days, undo, redo, and relaunch leave the block exactly once in the expected saved file and rendered day.
contracts.authority: Tine E-B2 destination-before-source hold-barrier and undo durability

acceptableVariations: Journal styling and shortcut feedback may vary while the moved block remains durably owned by the expected day.
nonRequirements: Exact block position within the destination day, pixel geometry, or save timing.

contracts.userOutcome: Native journeys can wait for the expected persisted file contents before checking user outcomes.

acceptableVariations: Filesystem polling intervals and save latency may vary.
nonRequirements: An end-user journey by itself.

contracts.userOutcome: First-block aliases and page properties remain editable, persist, and resolve their page.

acceptableVariations: Autocomplete ranking and editor layout may evolve while the saved alias still resolves the page.
nonRequirements: Exact picker dimensions, animation, or DOM shape.

contracts.userOutcome: Zooming into a block by its bullet and jumping to a block from Ctrl-K leave the page file byte-for-byte unchanged, and after a restart the zoomed block is restored while the file is still unchanged.
contracts.authority: Browsing must never mutate the user's graph (GH #623): a Logseq graph is shared with other tools and sync, so a stamped id:: is an unwanted file change.

acceptableVariations: Which navigation entry reaches the block (bullet click or Ctrl-K), as long as the block ends up zoomed.
Timing of the session write, which is awaited by polling for the recorded position.
nonRequirements: Exact breadcrumb markup or zoom animation.
How the session encodes an ID-less block, only that the page file is not changed.
Startup toasts unrelated to navigation.

contracts.userOutcome: Embedded blocks keep local disclosure, keyboard navigation, deletion, and caret ownership in the visible embed.

acceptableVariations: Embed styling and control placement may evolve without changing the focused editing surface.
nonRequirements: Exact indentation pixels or disclosure-icon artwork.

contracts.userOutcome: Copy block ref gives a fresh target one durable identity; a pasted reference updates its badge and referrer panel before reload, survives reload, and follows later source changes.
The ((uuid)) that Copy block ref puts on the native clipboard names an id:: already present in the target's file at the moment the reference becomes available.
contracts.authority: og batch 10 durable block-ref receipt (id persisted before the reference is handed out)

acceptableVariations: Refresh timing may vary within the completed save lifecycle.
nonRequirements: Exact badge typography, panel layout, animation, or generated UUID value.

contracts.userOutcome: Escape and arrow keys transition between editing and block selection without losing the live selection.

acceptableVariations: Selection affordance styling may evolve while keyboard ownership remains intact.
nonRequirements: Exact selection highlight color or transition timing.

acceptableVariations: WebDriver may attach initially to any WebView and enumerate its handles in any order.

contracts.userOutcome: The E2E runner can discover native-driver capabilities and retain browser-specific evidence.

acceptableVariations: Driver feature detection may vary by supported platform and browser version.
nonRequirements: Any end-user product workflow by itself.

contracts.userOutcome: Quick Capture waits for its graph on a cold --capture launch, activates, accepts first-show typing, saves the journal entry, and supports a safe second-instance handoff.

acceptableVariations: Native focus timing and frame decoration may vary by window manager.
nonRequirements: Exact window position, border pixels, or focus-animation timing.

acceptableVariations: any OS/engine transformation that normalize() equates

Keeping rendered content mounted during a text-selection drag.

acceptableVariations: Empty-state wording and tab presentation may evolve.

Panel wording, list layout, or snapshot directory naming beyond the pre-journal-rename tag.

contracts.userOutcome: Future journals stay out of the feed while remaining directly reachable without changing their file bytes.

acceptableVariations: Feed ordering and date formatting may evolve around the inclusion boundary.

nonRequirements: Exact playback controls, waveform styling, or decoder implementation.

contracts.userOutcome: On compact viewports, sidebars behave as modal overlays with safe dismissal.

A PDF may be a routed split-pane tab while remaining contained beside the persistent sidebar.
nonRequirements: Exact breakpoint pixel value, drawer width, overlay opacity, or transition duration.
The PDF being an immediate child of the workspace element.

contracts.userOutcome: One app process keeps two graph windows distinct and routes Quick Capture to the intended open graph.
An edit still unsaved when a window switches to another graph lands in the graph it was typed in, never in the new graph, and no old-graph content paints into the switched window.
contracts.authority: I-20 late landing (og batches 7-10)

acceptableVariations: Window placement and OS activation order may vary while graph routing remains correct.
The switch may save the pending edit before or after the new graph paints, and the switched window may show any route of the new graph.
nonRequirements: Exact native window coordinates or stacking order.

contracts.userOutcome: A native Linux titlebar close uses Tine's safe persistence path and closes the real window.

acceptableVariations: Window-manager decoration details and button geometry may vary.
nonRequirements: Exact titlebar theme, icon size, or frame border width.

contracts.userOutcome: Slash page and tag references can be authored, selected, rendered, and persisted through the real editor.

acceptableVariations: Completion ranking and popup layout may evolve while explicit reference authoring remains intact; Query may use one command opening the visual sheet.
nonRequirements: Exact popup dimensions, suggestion order for unrelated items, DOM structure, or successful capture of a supplemental reload screenshot after the text and disk assertions pass.

contracts.userOutcome: The published Guide offers no New page or Settings control, and ?static=1 keeps the static site.

acceptableVariations: Guide page wording, layout and styling may change while the permalink, baked query rows, missing write controls and static fallback hold.

contracts.userOutcome: The outline guide toggles collapsible descendants in one accessible action and preserves the parent state.

acceptableVariations: Guide visual treatment and control placement may evolve.

nonRequirements: Exact menu order, iconography, or external application launch behavior.

contracts.userOutcome: Page property actions preserve literal header structure through edit, guarded save, reload, and keyboard traversal.

acceptableVariations: Panel layout and native form-control styling may evolve.

nonRequirements: Exact section spacing, control dimensions, or debounce timing.
A fixed five-preset-only Tab sequence.

contracts.userOutcome: The quiet target below page content always adds a new writable trailing block, even when the page already ends in an empty (possibly indented) bullet.

acceptableVariations: Target affordance styling and scroll position may evolve.
nonRequirements: Exact target height, cursor blink timing, or focus-ring style.

contracts.userOutcome: PDF highlights, links, annotations, outline destinations, and restored view state interoperate with Logseq data.
PDF asset switches and target navigation isolate reader state without crashes or runaway resource use.
contracts.authority: Tine PDF interoperability and reader resource-safety contract

acceptableVariations: Reader layout, coordinate normalization, theme presentation, and annotation menu placement may evolve while the persisted interoperability outcomes remain intact.
Reader tools may move from the toolbar into a visible overflow menu in narrow panes.
Highlight references may open in a companion notes tab; returning to Journals need not use Back history.
Closing one PDF resource may reveal a different retained PDF tab.
nonRequirements: Exact drag threshold.
Exact theme palette/RGB.
Exact CSS filter/DOM strategy.
Outline and Area being direct toolbar buttons at every pane width.
A newly opened notes tab inheriting journal back-history.
Closing one reader leaving no other PDF viewer mounted.

acceptableVariations: PDF rendering and graph-switch presentation may vary while the old graph is drained, the viewer is remounted, and sidecar bytes remain owner-isolated.

contracts.userOutcome: Signed community plugin and theme metadata remains bound to the reviewed package identity, and executable plugins install disabled until explicitly enabled.

contracts.userOutcome: Users can inspect safety evidence, install, enable, configure, and uninstall a community plugin or theme on desktop and compact settings layouts.

acceptableVariations: Catalogue card layout, explanatory wording, and settings geometry may evolve while provenance, review state, lifecycle controls, and compact usability remain available.
nonRequirements: Exact screenshot pixels, toast stacking, card dimensions, or animation timing.

contracts.userOutcome: A persisted enabled plugin activates under a verified non-revoking cache, while a verified cached revocation retains its exact signed envelope, prevents every guest contribution, durably disables the installed version, and keeps it disabled after later cache unavailability.
contracts.authority: Tine signed plugin launch-revocation and cache-atomicity contract

acceptableVariations: The reserved signed fixture may use a host-owned command or thread-lines block-decoration contribution, provided the positive control makes activation observable.
Catalogue wording and settings-row presentation may vary while the native envelope, disable bit, and non-execution outcomes remain exact.

contracts.authority: Tine host-only plugin graph generation and editor ownership contract

acceptableVariations: Plugin command presentation and graph-switch animation may evolve while stale effects stay inert and the current-graph positive control persists normally.
nonRequirements: Exact worker delay, DOM nesting, switch timing, or plugin cancellation.

contracts.userOutcome: Page-menu PDF export creates only a static, script-disabled print frame.
contracts.authority: Tine print-export script isolation contract

acceptableVariations: Platform print integration and visual page layout may vary after the isolated frame is created.
nonRequirements: Exact print-dialog appearance, paper margins, or font rasterization.

contracts.userOutcome: Generated sites preserve source capability, safe URL handling, contextual anchors, and CSP at the export boundary.
contracts.authority: Tine published-site capability and CSP contract

acceptableVariations: Generated markup organization and browser rendering may vary while the security boundary holds.
nonRequirements: Exact generated whitespace, CSS class names, or visual theme.

contracts.userOutcome: Graph search, query workspaces, references, evidence, filters, and materialization preserve their visible query state.

acceptableVariations: Result presentation and pane layout may evolve while membership, predicates, evidence, and safe materialization remain correct; a highlighted unlinked mention may itself open and select the exact source occurrence without a redundant numbered jump row.
nonRequirements: Exact row heights, result-card DOM structure, or tab animation.

contracts.userOutcome: A query block rests as one sentence and answers with blocks or, for a page-level filter, pages; a query the engine cannot read shows what it did not understand instead of an empty result, and an empty result explains which condition emptied it.

A query created with /query and saved from the sheet's query text lands in the page file as an ordinary query block without touching the other query blocks, and reopens with the same answers after a restart.

acceptableVariations: The sentence wording, the macro name the engine prints (query or tine-query) and the why-empty table layout may evolve while the query and its answers stay the same; offscreen result groups may hydrate when scrolled into view.
nonRequirements: Sheet geometry, animation, or the order of rows inside the why-empty table.

contracts.userOutcome: With a query's builder sheet open, real pointer presses and key presses on the sheet's own controls (the + Add condition button, the field chooser's filter and rows, its operator list) act on the sheet: the block behind does not enter edit mode, the sheet stays open, typed keys reach the filter, and Escape peels the chooser then the sheet without editing or changing any other block.
The sheet opens next to the query sentence it belongs to and the field chooser's rows are readable and on screen.

acceptableVariations: Which side of the sentence the sheet opens on, the chooser's row height, the wording of rows and operators, and how many Escape presses it takes while the chooser and sheet are both open.
nonRequirements: Exact sheet or popover geometry, animation, or the order of fields in the chooser.

contracts.userOutcome: Renaming a page updates the real graph and keeps linked-reference behavior coherent.

A page whose title:: differs from its filename is found and renamed by its title: the file moves to the new title's name, title:: and every [[title]] reference are rewritten, and the filename is not offered as a separate page.

Renaming onto an existing page asks for confirmation; declining leaves every file byte-identical, accepting merges the source into the survivor (aliases and blocks), rewrites references, and keeps the source's exact bytes recoverable once.
contracts.authority: og rename-merge contract (batches 8/12); title-owned rename bytes equal master (og 11e)

contracts.userOutcome: After a rename or merge the user is on the renamed or surviving page, whatever page they came from.

acceptableVariations: Navigation timing and rendered reference layout may vary after rename.
The merged alias order and the trash location of the source copy may vary while both aliases survive and exactly one copy of the source bytes remains under logseq/.
nonRequirements: Exact file-list ordering or transition animation.
The wording or button labels of the native merge confirmation.

contracts.userOutcome: Right-sidebar disclosures, bulk controls, edit-safe unmounting, and restart restoration retain their state correctly.

contracts.userOutcome: On a phone, a left-edge swipe opens the left drawer (on iOS, with history to pop, it goes Back instead), while short, vertical or mid-screen swipes do nothing.
Swiping a block right indents it, swiping it left outdents it or opens its action menu, and the result is saved to the page file; short or vertical swipes change nothing.

acceptableVariations: Thresholds, snap-back animation, finger-tracking feel and swipe distances may evolve; blocking is that a deliberate swipe does the action and a clearly short or vertical one does not.
The action-bar analogue may be a different menu or toolbar as long as it selects the block and offers its actions.
nonRequirements: Exact pixel thresholds, animation timing or haptics.
The OS delivering real touches: this journey injects synthetic touch events into the WebKitGTK webview.
Android hardware Back, which is an OS gesture covered by unit tests and a device check.
